sources_considered.why: This is the only source found that estimates deployed Blackwell packages against the roughly 3 million shipped. It is a model from a GPU-finance firm and rests on assumed staging lags.
Primary NVIDIA transcript. It gives the hyperscaler deployment rate per week. It is dated May 2025, before the target period, and 'deploying' may mean taking delivery, so it is context only.
Nadella says some Microsoft GPUs sit uninstalled. This partly supports the warehouse thesis, but he gives no count.
Analyst summary of NVIDIA's May 2026 call. Its 'hundreds of thousands deployed' remark covers only some customers, is vague, and comes after the post date. Context only.
An anonymous Substack that infers Meta stockpiling from balance-sheet construction-in-progress. It is speculative and gives no installed-count total.
The speaker's own post. Read only for context on the 3 million figure, and not cited as evidence.
Reports the State of AI estimate covering only named GB200/GB300 projects as of July 2025. That is outside the target period and a partial scope.

evidence_items.locator: FAQ, 'How many Blackwell GPUs are actually deployed and clustered?'

receipt.public_excerpt: Of the 2.88 million deployed packages, about a third (0.98 million) run as standalone nodes or micro-clusters rather than in 256-plus GPU clusters.

evidence_items.explanation: Estimates about 2.88 million of 3.2 million Blackwell packages were deployed at end-2025, well above 1.5 million. But this is a model. The staging share is an assumption, not a measured count.

receipt.public_excerpt: Earlier quarterly cohorts deployed fully. The weighted lag across the installed base is approximately 10 percent.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the deployed figure in e1 rests on an assumption that earlier shipment cohorts 'deployed fully', not on an observed census. This weakens e1 as decisive evidence.

evidence_items.locator: paragraph quoting Nadella from BG2 Pod

receipt.public_excerpt: you may actually have a bunch of chips sitting in inventory that I can’t plug in. In fact, that is my problem today.

evidence_items.explanation: Nadella confirmed that some of Microsoft's GPUs were sitting uninstalled for lack of powered buildings. That fits part of the speaker's thesis, but it gives no count and no Blackwell share.

receipt.public_excerpt:
On average, major hyperscalers are each deploying nearly 1,000 NVL72 racks or 72,000 Blackwell GPUs per
week and are on track to further ramp output this quarter.

evidence_items.explanation: NVIDIA claimed a very high deployment rate per hyperscaler. If 'deploying' meant installing, it would imply well over 1.5 million installed within months. But the wording may describe deliveries, and the statement predates the target period.

unresolved_gaps: No independent census or measured count of installed Blackwell packages as of May 2026 was found.
The only direct estimate against the claim (e1) comes from a GPU-finance firm. It assumes, rather than observes, that earlier shipments deployed fully.
NVIDIA's 'deploying' language (e4) does not clearly separate installation from delivery.
No hyperscaler disclosed installed Blackwell unit counts that add up to a figure comparable with 1.5 million.
Nadella's comment (e3) confirms some GPUs sat uninstalled but gives no quantity.
